title: SOLID Principles
description: The five object-oriented design principles and the specific maintenance pain each one prevents.
learning_objectives: State each principle and the failure mode it addresses
Identify single-responsibility violations in an existing class
Explain why depending on abstractions reduces coupling

title: Encapsulation and Information Hiding
description: Designing class boundaries so internal representation can change without breaking callers.
learning_objectives: Choose an interface that hides implementation detail
Recognise when getters/setters are an anti-pattern
Decide what belongs in the public surface of a class

title: Cohesion and Coupling
description: The two metrics that predict how expensive a codebase is to change.
learning_objectives: Distinguish high cohesion from low coupling in a design
Use dependency direction to reduce ripple effects
Diagnose a design that is hard to unit test

title: UML Class and Sequence Diagrams
description: Communicating a design on a whiteboard during an interview using standard notation.
learning_objectives: Draw a class diagram with correct relationship notation
Model a runtime interaction as a sequence diagram
Use diagrams to justify a design decision

title: Interfaces, Abstract Classes and Composition
description: Choosing between inheritance and composition, and knowing when each is wrong.
learning_objectives: Prefer composition over inheritance where behaviour varies
Explain the fragile base class problem
Decide between an interface and an abstract class

title: Singleton Pattern
description: Controlling instance count, and why this pattern is usually better replaced by dependency injection.
learning_objectives: Implement a thread-safe singleton
Explain the testing problems a singleton introduces
Offer a cleaner alternative using injection

title: Factory and Abstract Factory
description: Centralising object creation so callers depend on an interface rather than a concrete type.
learning_objectives: Refactor scattered construction into a factory
Decide when an abstract factory earns its complexity
Keep creation logic out of domain objects

title: Builder Pattern
description: Constructing complex objects step by step, avoiding telescoping constructors.
learning_objectives: Replace a constructor with many optional parameters
Decide between a builder and named arguments
Enforce required fields at build time

title: Strategy Pattern
description: Swapping interchangeable algorithms at runtime without branching inside the caller.
learning_objectives: Replace a growing if/switch ladder with strategies
Keep strategies stateless where possible
Select a strategy from configuration or input

title: Observer Pattern
description: Publishing state changes to interested parties without tight coupling.
learning_objectives: Design a publish/subscribe relationship
Handle unsubscribe and failure of a subscriber
Recognise the memory-leak risk of strong references

title: Decorator Pattern
description: Adding behaviour by wrapping rather than subclassing, and composing wrappers freely.
learning_objectives: Wrap an object to add cross-cutting behaviour
Compare decorator with inheritance for behaviour stacking
Order decorators correctly when they interact

title: Adapter and Facade
description: Making incompatible interfaces work together, and simplifying a complex subsystem behind one entry point.
learning_objectives: Wrap a third-party API behind your own interface
Distinguish adapter (compatibility) from facade (simplification)
Isolate vendor changes to one class

title: Command Pattern
description: Representing an action as an object, enabling undo, queuing and logging.
learning_objectives: Encapsulate a request as an object
Implement undo by pairing execute with revert
Queue or log commands for replay

title: State Pattern
description: Modelling an object whose behaviour changes with its internal state.
learning_objectives: Replace state-dependent branching with state objects
Define legal transitions explicitly
Avoid invalid states by construction

title: Parking Lot
description: The classic LLD warm-up: model floors, spots, vehicles, ticketing and payment.
learning_objectives: Derive core entities from the requirements before coding
Assign spot types to vehicle types with correct semantics
Make fee calculation extensible for future pricing rules

title: BookMyShow / Movie Ticket Booking
description: Seat inventory, concurrent booking, temporary holds and payment failure recovery.
learning_objectives: Prevent double-booking under concurrency
Model a seat hold with expiry
Recover cleanly when payment fails after a hold

title: Splitwise / Expense Sharing
description: Groups, unequal splits, balances and debt simplification.
learning_objectives: Model split strategies (equal, exact, percentage, shares)
Maintain consistent balances on every mutation
Simplify a debt graph into fewer settlements

title: Food Delivery (Zomato / Swiggy)
description: Restaurant menus, cart, order lifecycle, assignment and delivery tracking.
learning_objectives: Model the order state machine end to end
Assign a delivery partner fairly and consistently
Handle cancellation and refund at each lifecycle stage

title: Chess Game
description: Board, pieces, legal move generation, check and checkmate detection.
learning_objectives: Model pieces with polymorphic move rules
Keep move validation separate from movement
Detect check without duplicating rule logic

title: Rate Limiter
description: Token bucket, sliding window and fixed window, with the trade-offs of each.
learning_objectives: Implement a token-bucket limiter that is thread-safe
Compare fixed and sliding windows for burst behaviour
Decide between in-process and shared-state limiting
